source.title: On the Convergence Rate of Training Recurrent Neural Networks
source.authors: Zeyuan Allen-Zhu; Yuanzhi Li; Zhao Song

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence results for overparameterized recurrent networks, a new setting for the broad training-convergence claim, but tests none of the listed version-specific behaviors or benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The results are theoretical guarantees for regression loss on δ-separable training sequences, not CIFAR classification results. Cited empirical and theoretical findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence for overparameterized ReLU RNNs on sequence regression. Its own results do not test any listed version: recurrent regression convergence does not measure CIFAR convolutional classification error, teacher-student minima frequencies, or the specified depth, initialization, learning-rate or normalization comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors prove high-probability linear convergence of GD and SGD to ε regression loss at output positions 2 through L under sufficient overparameterization and data separability, with polynomial dependence on sequence length. They establish avoidance of bad local minima along these training trajectories, without excluding their existence elsewhere.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical convergence guarantees for recurrent regression networks under separability and width assumptions; it does not run the benchmark classification recipes named in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on overparameterization and δ-separability; the paper does not compare alternative settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1 and 2 guarantee arbitrarily small sequence regression loss with high probability for sufficiently wide ReLU Elman RNNs, training W from Gaussian initialization while fixing A and B, under the stated separability assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently overparameterized ReLU RNNs admit GD and SGD convergence to ε training regression loss in iterations polynomial in sequence length and logarithmic in 1/ε.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4 and Appendix B establish polynomial signal-propagation bounds for the specified Gaussian-initialized ReLU RNNs; they do not compare initialization choices or establish a training-speed advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under sufficient overparameterization, the specified Gaussian initialization and ReLU recurrence avoid exponential signal explosion or vanishing in sequence length.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and rely on strong width and data-separability assumptions. They do not report empirical runs or classification error.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained on CIFAR-10/100 classification, including random labels and the stated size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks or Fixup.
Whether alternative initializations change training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Training above or below an initial stability threshold, transient loss increases, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Here ρ = nLd log m and ϱ = nLdδ^−1 log(m/ε). Theoretical convergence results are eligible evidence in principle; exclusion here follows from their mismatch with the specified claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons across model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima frequency, and extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual shortcut networks and depth-dependent classification error.
Comparisons of initializations, training speed, or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability limit, loss rises, curvature, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

rows.subject: Elman RNN with ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 1 gives a gradient descent convergence guarantee while optimizing W; A and B remain at random initialization.

conditions.value: n training sequences of length L; first inputs are δ-separable
m ≥ C̄ⁱ, with C and ̄ as defined in Theorem 1

rows.note: The theorem states a guarantee, not an empirical measurement; its error measure is regression loss, not classification error.
rows.check: The regression guarantee is valid but cannot establish any listed version's effect. Correct the corrupted width condition to m ≥ C·ϱ^C and the GD step size to η = δ/(ρ^44 m). Appendix H gives T ∈ [ρ^59 log(1/ε)/δ², ρ^59 ϱ^28 log(1/ε)/δ²], not the recorded interval. The loss covers output positions 2 through L; A and B remain fixed.
